entries.mechanism: Origins: 235 countries. Axiom's section_122_component_rate is 0 on this 232-metal line: the chapter 99 US note for the section 122 surcharge excludes 232-covered articles ('7202.11.10' exclusion, HTS ch.99 page-226; 'articles of aluminum, of steel, or of copper ... headings 9903.82.02 and 9903.82.04', page-230), encoded with proof atoms in rulespec-us us/policies/cbp/us-tariff-duty/composition.yaml (section_122_component_rate: 'if entry_is_line_a or entry_is_line_b: 0'). The Yale statutory layer deliberately keeps the literal 10% in statutory_rate_s122 and scopes the 232 overlap at the effective layer instead (metal-content shares; nonmetal_share forced to 0 post-annex): docs/statutory_deviations.md taxonomy ('applicability ... statutory_rate_* keeps the literal-enumeration rate') and docs/assumptions.md 'Section 122 effective contribution' at Budget-Lab-Yale/tariff-rate-tracker@c4307e514196618afcbf88cf7fd33746417eeabf.

Origins: 140 countries. Yale's legal-date panel zeroes every IEEPA statutory rate from 2026-02-20, the SCOTUS ruling date (Learning Resources v. Trump): config/policy_params.yaml ieepa_invalidation_policy_date '2026-02-20' ('overridden to 2026-02-20 when use_policy_dates=TRUE') and docs/policy_timing.md ('IEEPA invalidation is modeled on the ruling date') at Budget-Lab-Yale/tariff-rate-tracker@c4307e514196618afcbf88cf7fd33746417eeabf. Axiom encodes the CBP/Federal Register termination effective 2026-02-24 (FR 2026-03832; ieepa_component_rate switches to the terminated rate at 02-24), so the 02-20 and 02-23 probes carry our still-active IEEPA rate against their zero. Timing-convention boundary between the ruling date and the implementation date.

Origins: 139 countries. Axiom's ieepa_component_rate is 0 on this 232-metal line for reciprocal-tariff origins (or carries only the china fentanyl 10%, which is not metals-excluded): the encoded reciprocal exclusions (proof atoms in composition.yaml ieepa_component_rate, including the metal-article exclusions) remove 232-covered articles from the reciprocal duty. Yale's statutory layer keeps the origin's reciprocal/floor rate in statutory_rate_ieepa_recip on these lines and resolves the 232 overlap downstream at the effective layer (docs/statutory_deviations.md: the statutory layer keeps the unclaimed/literal rate; EU floor entries store the 15% floor minus the statutory MFN base) at Budget-Lab-Yale/tariff-rate-tracker@c4307e514196618afcbf88cf7fd33746417eeabf.

Origins: BY, CU, KP, RU. Axiom applies the HTS column 2 rate for General Note 3(b) countries (KP/BY/RU/CU): composition.yaml origin_is_column_2_country with the GN3(b) proof atom, and for Russian-origin 7601.10.30 the 70% heading 9903.90.09 rate in lieu of column 2 (ch.99 US note 30(c), page-508). The Yale panel's statutory_base_rate is parsed exclusively from the HTS column-1 'general' field (src/pipeline/04_parse_products.R, parse_rate(general)); the column-2 'other' field is never read and no GN3(b) branch exists, so column-2 origins carry the column-1 rate. Reference-side gap, not listed in their statutory_deviations registry, at Budget-Lab-Yale/tariff-rate-tracker@c4307e514196618afcbf88cf7fd33746417eeabf.
